pull: Clue: Only Chicago had one before it
body:
Can you name this machine?

On 4 November 1943, at a secret wartime site in Tennessee, it went critical for the first time. Behind its concrete face sat a 24 foot cube of graphite, and workers pushed uranium slugs into the holes with long rods. Its job was to prove America could make plutonium.

The clue is on the card. Drop your guess below.
photoNote: Workers using a rod to push uranium slugs into the loading face of the X-10 Graphite Reactor at Oak Ridge, about 1943. Photo by Ed Westcott, U.S. Army Manhattan Engineer District, via the American Museum of Science and Energy. Public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government. Wartime, but not dated to the day of criticality.
photoCredit: Workers loading uranium slugs into the face of the X-10 Graphite Reactor, Oak Ridge, Tennessee, about 1943. Ed Westcott, Manhattan Engineer District, public domain.
